title: Elodie and the Autopsy
premise: Felix Crane, a meticulous hotel concierge and unofficial fixer, is hired by a nervous woman named Elodie Vasseur who pays triple to prove that a murder scheduled to happen at the hotel in nine days will not occur — the victim, according to an anonymous dossier she received, is Elodie herself. As Felix investigates, the dossier's predictions begin coming true with eerie precision, suggesting the killer has access to Felix's own methods and records. The trail leads to a decades-old cover-up involving the hotel's founding family and Elodie's true identity as the hidden heir everyone believed dead. In the end Felix must choose between protecting her client by exposing the truth and preserving the hotel's fragile peace, trapping the killer — the family's trusted lawyer — in a staged 'autopsy' of the crime before it happens.
about_author: Dominic Brightwater is a former night-shift concierge who spent eleven years watching guests lie beautifully in marble lobbies. He writes mysteries from a rented room above a shuttered grand hotel, where he still keeps the old guest ledger for inspiration.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A pale woman named Elodie Vasseur arrives at the concierge desk with a thick envelope and a stranger's dossier predicting her murder in nine days. Felix, who never takes a case she can't close, accepts against instinct. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Nine Days on the Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She audits the dossier against hotel records and finds three predictions already fulfilled — a room booking, a staff transfer, a cancelled inspection. Someone is orchestrating events inside the hotel itself. Beat: dread replaces skepticism.

chapters.title: Elodie's Empty Suitcase
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie unpacks almost nothing; she travels like someone expecting to leave in a hurry or not at all. Fragments surface of an orphanage childhood and a locket she won't explain. Beat: loneliness and guarded hope.

chapters.title: The Concierge Who Notices Everything
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix works her network — doormen, cleaners, a retired police archivist — and learns the dossier's language mirrors her own private case notes, word for word. Beat: violation; the hunter realizes she is also being watched.

chapters.title: Room 704
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The dossier names Room 704 as the murder site. Felix finds it freshly renovated over a sealed older suite, its floor plan altered years ago. Beat: the past literally built over, hidden in plain sight.

chapters.title: The Founding Family
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Research into the hotel's owners, the Marchetti dynasty, reveals a granddaughter declared dead thirty years ago after a fire. The timeline matches Elodie's birthdate. Beat: the case stops being about a prediction and becomes about identity.

chapters.title: What Elodie Remembers
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Confronted gently, Elodie recalls fragments: smoke, a woman singing in French, hands passing her through a window. She admits she came to the hotel because the dossier told her to. Beat: terror and longing entwined — she wants to belong somewhere, even here.

chapters.title: Day Five: The First Attempt
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A staged accident nearly crushes Elodie in the service elevator; Felix pulls her clear. The near-miss proves the killer is improvising ahead of schedule. Beat: fear becomes urgency; the clock accelerates.

chapters.title: The Lawyer Who Never Leaves
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Suspicion falls on Aurelio Marchetti's counsel, Silas Renner, who has managed the family's affairs for four decades and signed every document sealing the fire's record. But his alibis are immaculate. Beat: frustration; the obvious suspect is too clean.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Felix and Elodie, running out of safe ground, share a quiet night in the closed rooftop bar — confessions, near-tenderness, an unspoken agreement not to name it while one of them may die. Beat: warmth sharpened by mortality.

chapters.title: The Second Dossier
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A second dossier appears in Felix's own locker, this time predicting HER interference and its cost. The killer knows her playbook because it was once taught to someone close to her. Beat: betrayal foreshadowed.

chapters.title: The Apprentice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix traces the phrasing to Tomas, her former protégé, now head of hotel security — hired two years ago by Renner. Tomas swears he only wrote observations, never plans. Beat: heartbreak and doubt; loyalty under interrogation.

chapters.title: Day Seven: The Sealed Suite
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie breaks into the original suite behind Room 704 and finds a child's room preserved in dust — hers. Photographs, a hospital bracelet, proof she was smuggled out alive. Beat: grief and vindication colliding.

chapters.title: The Fire, Retold
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Reconstructing the old fire, Felix finds the official story impossible: the nursery door was locked from outside. Someone wanted the heir dead then, and someone wants the secret buried now. Beat: cold clarity; the shape of the conspiracy emerges.

chapters.title: Renner's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix corners Renner; he admits the family paid to erase the heir but denies ordering murder — then is found unconscious before he can name his principal. Beat: the truth snatched away at the last second.

chapters.title: Day Eight: The Trap Is Set
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Realizing the final dossier entry predicts an 'autopsy' — a post-mortem examination of the crime — Felix decides to stage the murder scene early, complete and convincing, forcing the killer to come correct the record. Beat: resolve; the hunted becomes architect.

chapters.title: The Autopsy of a Murder
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In Room 704, Felix lays out the fake scene with Elodie playing the victim. Hidden witnesses watch. The killer arrives to adjust details only the true murderer would know — and it is the beloved night manager, Marguerite, the woman who smuggled Elodie out and was promised silence, now cleaning up the last loose end. Beat: shock and sorrow.

chapters.title: Why She Stayed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's confession, framed through Felix's POV. Marguerite killed to protect the family's bargain that kept her employed and Elodie hidden — love twisted into duty into murder. Beat: tragic understanding without forgiveness.

chapters.title: Day Nine: What Was Supposed to Happen
chapters.summary: Climax. Marguerite escapes custody briefly and confronts Elodie in the preserved suite; Elodie, choosing truth over vengeance, talks her down as police arrive. Beat: Elodie claims her own story at last.

chapters.title: The Heir of the House
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Press, lawyers, and the dying patriarch converge; Elodie must decide whether to claim the Marchetti name. She signs nothing, keeping her own. Beat: belonging defined on her own terms.

chapters.title: Closing the Case File
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix closes the file — the first case she solved before the crime occurred — and burns the dossiers. Tomas asks to be forgiven; she gives him work, not absolution. Beat: bittersweet restoration of order.

chapters.title: Checkout Time
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Weeks later, Elodie checks out of the hotel — and immediately checks back in, as a guest choosing to stay. On the rooftop bar, she and Felix finally name what they are to each other. Beat: quiet joy; love chosen freely, duty laid down.
